issues.legal_issue: A daughter’s birth before the original succession legislation does not by itself exclude her from succession to a deceased coparcener’s interest when a female relative specified as a Class I heir survives him.
material_facts: The coparcener died in 2001, leaving two daughters, two sons and a widow.
The properties were found to be joint family properties, and the daughters were denied shares on the ground that they had been born before the original succession legislation.
issues.conclusion: The deceased coparcener’s interest did not pass by survivorship alone. It had to be ascertained by a notional partition immediately before his death and devolved by succession on his heirs, including the surviving female heirs specified in Class I.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 6 and Explanation 1 of the Hindu Succession Act as it stood before the 2005 amendment, if a Mitakshara coparcener died leaving a Class I female relative, his interest devolved by testamentary or intestate succession rather than survivorship. Explanation 1 required a notional partition to ascertain that interest. The Court relied on Anar Devi v. Parmeshwari Devi and the interpretation of Explanation 1 in Mulla, Principles of Hindu Law.

predicates.partition_suit: A party brought a suit seeking partition of property held by a joint family.
predicates.coparcener_died_after_succession_law_com: A coparcener died after the succession law had commenced.
predicates.surviving_class_one_female_heir: A female heir specified in the first class of heirs survived the coparcener.

issues.definition: When a partition suit concerns coparcenary property and a coparcener dies after the succession law has commenced leaving a surviving female heir in the first class of heirs, the deceased’s interest is ascertained by notional partition and devolves by succession.

issues.legal_issue: Daughters born before the 2005 amendment may receive the same coparcenary share as sons when the amendment takes effect while a partition suit remains pending and the partition has not become final.
material_facts: The two daughters were born before the original succession legislation and their father died in 2001.
They claimed shares in properties found to belong to the joint family.
The partition suit was filed in 2002, but the trial court’s decree was passed in 2007, after the 2005 amendment had taken effect.
The Court found that the daughters were entitled to shares and directed that the partition decree be drawn accordingly.
issues.conclusion: The daughters were entitled to equal shares as coparceners, notwithstanding their birth before the original legislation. Because the partition suit remained pending when the amendment took effect and the partition was not final, their rights had to be reflected in the partition decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, as amended in 2005, makes a daughter a coparcener by birth in the same manner as a son, with the same rights and liabilities; Section 6(3) provides for equal allotment to daughters and sons on a deemed partition. The Court relied on Prakash v. Phulavati for the application of the amendment irrespective of when daughters were born, and on Ganduri Koteshwaramma v. Chakiri Yanadi for the rule that daughters’ amended rights are not lost by a preliminary decree and may require its amendment before final partition. It also referred to State Bank of India v. Ghamandi Ram on coparcenary incidents, including the right to seek partition. The judgment recited Prakash’s holding concerning living daughters of living coparceners, but in this case treated the daughters’ rights as crystallized during the pending suit.

rule.if: partition_suit and coparcenary_property and amendment_took_effect_during_pending_suit and partition_not_final

predicates.partition_suit: A party brought a suit seeking partition of property held by a joint family.
predicates.coparcenary_property: The property in dispute was found to be coparcenary property.
predicates.amendment_took_effect_during_pending_sui: A legal amendment conferring equal coparcenary rights on daughters took effect while the partition suit was still pending.
predicates.partition_not_final: The partition had not become final when the amendment took effect.

issues.definition: If a partition suit over coparcenary property remains pending and the partition is not final when an amendment conferring equal rights on daughters takes effect, the daughters receive equal coparcenary shares as sons.
